Project Title: Augmentation of water supply at Doimukh Township.
Tender Name: Augmentation of water supply at Doimukh Township.
Brief Scope of Work: Water is currently supplied to Doimukh township from a water treatment plant at a rate of 1 MLD during the leanest period. The current population including the floating population of the town is around 9448 Nos. The existing treatment system is also based on old conventional methods which are proving to be incapable to treat water with high turbidity during monsoon season. Further, the current source from which water is tapped for Doimukh Township is depleting rapidly and the discharge of the source depletes to such a level during lean period that water availability becomes an issue in many pockets of Tezu township. Taking into consideration of all the above-mentioned issues, this scheme has been proposed to address the water scarcity in Doimukh Township. Under this project, it is proposed to provide water to Doimukh township by conjointly tapping a gravity-based surface source (Luksin source) in addition to the already existing gravity source (Heri Nallah). Further, the existing Slow Sand Filter is proposed to be converted/replaced with Rapid Sand Filter due to high rate of filtration.

Project Title: Water Supply to Kharsang Township
Tender Name: Water Supply to Kharsang Township
Brief Scope of Work: The Kharsang township has been declared recently as Urban town by the state government by seeing the rapid growth and development of the township. The town is located at low altitude and is unable to tap water directly from gravity sources due to non avilibality of gravity sources nearby area. The present water supply to Kharsang Town is of Lift water supply through Bore well which is partially covered with pipe water supply under JJM programe. The present water supply to the township is of 55 LPCD which is very less as per the prescribed 135 LPCD of the Urban towns which has a deficit of 80 LPCD. Now, the present population of the Town has been worked to be 3909 Nos. as per the population forecast method of Geometrical Increase Method for 80 LPCD excluding the population of institution, offices etc. and the said excluding population has been included in water requirement calculation as per LPCD provision given in the CPHEEO Mannual. The ultimate design population of the project town for design period of 30 years is 8191 Nos. Therefore, a new water supply project is necessary to cater the daily water requirements of the Town as well as the other Govt. institutions, offices and publice places etc. in the town and due to non availability of gravity sources, it has been decided that the water shall be tapped from Namphuk river having a sufficient discharge by constructing a Jack well and shall be conveyed through 250 mm dia. HDPE Pipe to meet up the water demand of 2.20 MLD. The main line is of 1.50 KM distance from the proposed intake point to the proposed WTP and after the execution of this project, the consumers of the Khasang town will be highly benefited. Hence, this project is proposed under AMRUT.

Replacement of existing PVC lines with HDPE lines in various Sectors of the city. Integration of STP Maloya in TT Water network. Project Title: STRENGTHENING, PROVIDING AND LAYING OF 250MM (10”) i/d SW PIPE SEWER LINE AT COLONIES IN SECTOR 25, CHANDIGARH
Tender Name: STRENGTHENING, PROVIDING AND LAYING OF 250MM (10”) i/d SW PIPE SEWER LINE AT COLONIES IN SECTOR 25, CHANDIGARH
Brief Scope of Work: MCC will spend around approx. Rs. 4.61 Crore for this work and it will be completed within 06 months. The population density in colonies (i.e. Janta Colony, Bhaskar Colony & Kumhar Colony) of Sector 25 had increased rapidly by 1.3 times within decade and is expected to reach from 27,000 to 36,664 by the year 2053. The existing sewerage system, consisting of 150 mm diameter sewer lines, has become incapable of handling the excess load of sewage generated by the native households. As a result, the sewerage is overflowing resulting into water borne diseases. This is also causing contamination in the drinking water. Moreover, in addition to increased population, the per capita consumption/supply of water (i.e. 245 LPCD, which is approx. 1.8 times more than Standard Norms set by the Govt, of India) also contributed towards excess generation of sewage/waste water as well. The Municipal Corporation Chandigarh on day to day basis is also facing difficulties during maintenance, addressing the complaints regarding blockages, overflowing, etc. This project aims to improve the sewerage system and to avoid inconveniences by replacing the rising 150 mm (6") to 200mm (8") dia lines with 200mm (8”) i/d and 250mm (10”) i/d dia sewer lines to take the increased flow which improves the overall sewerage network.
